title: Annotatio II §.VII open: Nativitas of both Consubstantiations reborn — Lateran XIII under Innocent III
pass_a_gloss: §. VII. So stands the Nativity of either Consubstantiation, born again in the 13th Century in the Lateran Council under Innocent III — which Council injects mention of Consubstantiation as an opinion already then exploded and antiquated, in these words:
pass_b_english: §.VII: both Consubstantiations have their Nativity reborn in the 13th century — Lateran Council under Innocent III.
That council already treats Consubstantiation as an exploded, antiquated opinion, and names it thus:
source_text: §. VII. Ita habet Nativitas utriusque Consubstantiationis, Seculo 13, in Concilio Lateranensi, sub Innocentio III., rursus denatae, quod Concilium, Consubstantiationis, ceu jam tum explosæ & antiquatæ opinionis, mentionem, hisce injicit:
